Morning at Noordwijkweg begins with careful listening. Birds call from the undergrowth, quick movements flicker along the forest edge, and the sun still leaves time for a leisurely outing before the heat sets in. Binoculars reveal the details of their plumage; sometimes the most colorful encounter happens during a brief stop beside the road.

Noordwijkweg is part of a birdwatching route in the vicinity of Paramaribo. Its forest edges and secondary vegetation are of particular interest. The excursion offers a chance to encounter tropical birds in their natural surroundings: moving quietly, taking breaks, and relying on an experienced accompanying guide all matter.

One of the goals of Ada Tours' morning outing in this area is to spot the red-bellied manakin with its vivid crimson cap. The group then continues to the coast at Weg naar Zee. Combining woodland and tidal shoreline makes it possible to explore different habitats in a single day. Sightings vary from visit to visit; lightweight, covering clothing and insect protection will help you focus on the walk.

North Plaza lies off the eastern coast of Santa Cruz. The underwater route follows a rocky slope that gradually gives way to a sandy seabed. Garden eels can be seen in the sandy areas, while reef fish swim above the rocks.

The dive-site description mentions whitetip reef sharks, rays, and sea lions. On the eastern side, divers may encounter pelagic animals, including hammerhead sharks and Galápagos sharks. According to the tour description, landing on North Plaza is closed to visitors; this visit involves diving off the island. South Plaza remains a separate destination.

Along the designated trails, visitors may see blue-footed boobies, frigatebirds, iguanas, and sea lions. The animals are often close to the path, but they should be observed without approaching or disturbing them. A visit to the island is often combined with the beaches of Bachas on Santa Cruz.

## Oaxaca — Mexico's History!

Oaxaca is an enchanting town that seems untouched by time.

## Oaxaca — a City for Discerning Travelers!

It is located in southern Mexico, in the Sierra Madre del Sur mountains, and was founded by Spanish settlers in 1532 during the colonial conquests. The city suits travelers who enjoy a relaxing holiday. Oaxaca and its surroundings are home to numerous archaeological monuments. Its excellent cuisine and beautiful handicrafts made by local artisans will appeal to even the most discerning visitors.

The Basilica of Ocotlán is instantly recognizable by its combination of red brick and white carved stucco. Two towers frame the facade, while the Baroque interior reveals its intricate decoration in the altars and the camarín, the shrine chamber associated with the revered image of Our Lady.

According to religious tradition, devotion to Our Lady of Ocotlán began after an apparition in 1541, and a wooden image was found inside a tree. The shrine remains a place of pilgrimage. It is worth pausing both at the main altar and in front of the facade to compare the richly decorated interior with the pale silhouette of the towers.
